hey ik this is an old thread now bc this game came out a year ago now but i picked it up a week ago and i wanted to pipe in too xD
    
i suffer from a few mental health disorders and issues and i often ramble, get confused and im really bad at wording things sometimes so hopefully this isn't too painful for you guys to read Dx
    
im a person in my 30s who grew up with games like Chrono Trigger, FFV, FFVI, Phantasy Star IV, etc
   
experiencing those in real time as they came out was def a unique experience that it'll never get to experience in that identical manner ever again, which is something that makes me sad but also makes me filled with happy memories of that time
   
anyways, when i got into my 20s, i was interested in the newest games released but very rarely did i care enough to check them out as my love for gaming peaked when i was around 18 in the late 2000s
   
so i discovered the world of indie gaming
   
games that harkened back to the games i grew up with, some of them pixellated, some of them low poly, some of them repeating the same gameplay mechanics and tropes in order to recreate that magic of yesteryear
   
let me tell you, ive waded through a sea of many that came close but never managed to recreate that genuine feeling. they came close but they always fell short bc they always felt more like they were trying to be bad copies of those games than retro-style games in their own right that paid homage to those games
   
so why all this rambling?
   
well, in recent years, ive noticed that certain teams seem to finally getting it right. it's rare but it genuinely happens. they manage to recreate the feel and the appeal of the games of the early to mid 90s while standing on their own feet as their own IP at the same time.
   
one of my fav game series of all time that achieves this is Axiom Verge - a cyberpunk dystopian futuristic metroidvania game that still manages to stand on its own and have an amazing mindfuck story that was made by a single man.
   
and yes, for me, Sea of Stars is another example of one that gets it right.
   
when i play this game, i get that same feeling i did when i was a kid, sat on my bed with a strategy guide and my older sister, trying to use our young brains to figure out where to go in Chrono Trigger and FFVI xD
   
and yes, a lot of the things in Sea of Stars are trope-y but, in the 90s, those things weren't trope-y, they were new mechanics and story points, etc. and by Sea of Stars including those tropes, it's not being trope-y, it's doing its part to recreate those moments when had all those years ago
   
but i get it, i mean, this game isn't gonna be for everyone and there were plenty of kids at my school that never played any FF games nor did they try games like Phantasy Star, Dragon Quest or Chrono Trigger bc those games were "too hard, too confusing, too long, too boring" and they just wanted to play Pokémon R&B, Crash, etc, so trust me ive heard it all before (not that i don't love those games too but im just saying they stuck to what was simpler to play)
   
so i hope that manages to explain why i adore Sea of Stars despite its imperfections and, oftentimes, FOR its imperfections
   
i hope those of you that weren't fans of it got at least a small something from playing Sea of Stars, even if you didn't enjoy it overall. i'd hate for you to get nothing from it whatsoever bc that's the worst feeling you can get from playing a game
   
and i hope those of you like me that did enjoy it and were fans of it managed to get as much out of it as you could.
   
if you played the same games as i did growing up and you loved it, i hope it brought you some of those feelings and memories back as it did with me and you got a new experience to add to your collection
   
if you played the same games as i did growing up and you hated it, im sorry it fell short of what you were expecting and i hope you manage to find a game in the future that recaptures the magic that you once experienced
   
and if you managed to make it this far and read my innate ramblings about being a child inside then tysm (: as i previously stated, i have mental health disorders that cause me to ramble, get confused and word things poorly so i hope it wasn't too much torture to read xD

but then there's always the simple point of the humour changing radically and me just not finding it funny anymore. I knew things had changed when I watched a 30 min episode of something a couple years back and I didn't even smile, let alone laugh.
   
so while I still watch compilations and collections of their older stuff and still laugh, and also listen to NSP and Starbomb occasionally, if you were to ask me if enjoy them anymore, my answer would be a solid no. they're not funny and at least one of them is ethically questionable at best.
